question: Should generic tool-progress intent be a supported public Plugin SDK capability whose channel renderers may fail closed by emitting only a reaction or no visible message?
rationale: The implementation is plausible, but this permanently expands third-party API and establishes a user-visible delivery policy that code review cannot infer without owner intent.

options.title: Approve and document the public contract
options.body: Define eligible producers, channel rendering and suppression semantics, compatibility expectations, and direct contract tests before merge.

options.title: Keep the marker internal
options.body: Carry the prepared fact only through bundled runtime internals and avoid exposing suppressible delivery semantics to third-party plugins.

options.title: Pause this approach
options.body: Hold or close the branch if maintainers do not want fail-closed transient progress to become a stable cross-plugin contract.

recommendation.title: Approve and document the public contract
recommendation.body: Define eligible producers, channel rendering and suppression semantics, compatibility expectations, and direct contract tests before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The current implementations of the three central surfaces all trace to their recent refactor commit.
